header.title: Text to Speech
header.description: Paste any text and hear it read aloud with natural voices. Adjust speed and pitch. Great for proofreading by ear or accessibility. Free — no tokens needed.

unsupported.hint: Please use Chrome, Edge, or Safari.

editor.title: Your Text
editor.placeholder: Paste your essay, article, or any text here to hear it read aloud. Great for catching errors your eyes might miss...

settings.title: Voice Settings
settings.proTip: Listening to your essay read aloud helps catch awkward phrasing, run-on sentences, and errors your eyes skip over.

voices.title: Multiple Voices
voices.description: Choose from Default, Male, or Female voice profiles. The browser selects the best available system voice for your chosen preference.

controls.title: Speed & Pitch Control
controls.description: Adjust playback speed from 0.5× to 2× and pitch from low to high to find the most comfortable listening experience.

free.title: Free — No Account Needed
free.description: Text to speech is completely free and requires no sign-in. No tokens are consumed, no limits on text length.

items.proofreading: Proofreading your writing by hearing it read back — your ears catch mistakes your eyes miss
items.accessibility: Making written content accessible to people with reading difficulties
items.scripts: Previewing how a script or narration sounds before recording
items.multitasking: Listening to articles or notes while doing something else
items.pronunciation: Language learners checking pronunciation of words and phrases

items.slowDown: Slow the speed to 0.75× when proofreading technical or complex content — it's easier to catch errors.
items.firstParagraph: Listen to the first paragraph at normal speed to check the flow, then scan the rest.
items.sections: For long text, paste one section at a time to keep the playback focused.
items.browser: If a voice sounds robotic, try a different browser — Chrome typically has the best voices.

free.question: Is text to speech free?
free.answer: Yes, completely free. It uses your browser's built-in SpeechSynthesis engine, so no tokens are consumed and no account is required.

devices.question: Why do the voices sound different on my phone versus my laptop?
devices.answer: Voices come from your device and operating system, not from our servers. Windows, macOS, Android, and iOS each ship different voices, so quality and selection vary by device.

controls.question: What do the rate and pitch controls do?
controls.answer: Rate controls how fast the text is read and pitch shifts the voice higher or lower. Both apply the next time you press play.

long.question: Can it read long documents?
long.answer: Yes. Long text is split into chunks behind the scenes, because some browsers cut off speech after a certain length. Playback continues seamlessly across chunks.

browsers.question: Which browsers are supported?
browsers.answer: Chrome, Edge, and Safari all support speech synthesis well. If you hear nothing, check your system volume and try a different voice from the list.
